deliverables: Secondary ticket marketplace with on-chain settlement
Custodial wallet onboarding for Sellout users
Public launch campaign and trade-show activations
Public metrics dashboard and quarterly reporting
request.recipient: Intersect as budget administrator for Anvil/Sellout delivery through the Sundae Labs TRSC/PSSC framework
request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Phase 2 of a Cardano-native ticketing platform operated by Sellout.io and built by Anvil Development Agency.

claims.claim: Phase 1 of the platform is already live on Cardano mainnet with on-chain event creation, CIP-68 ticket minting, transfers, and attendance verification funded by Sellout with over $130,000 of its own capital.
The proposal requests 4,969,231 ada, stated as about $1,093,231 at $0.22 per ADA, inclusive of a 3% Intersect administration fee, over 8 months.
Phase 2 is intended to deliver a secondary marketplace, royalty enforcement, anti-scalping controls, wallet onboarding, organizer tools, an independent audit, and launch amplification.
Sellout has 200,000+ registered users, has issued 250,000+ tickets, and runs 350+ events annually at its current cadence.
The proposal projects 12-month outcomes of 200+ events on-chain, 75,000+ CIP-68 NFT tickets, 150,000+ on-chain interactions, $6,000,000+ ticket revenue on-chain, and 20,000+ new wallets.
The Yellowstone Club 2026 concert series is presented as a contracted anchor deployment projected to move more than $6,000,000 through Cardano in year one.
The proposers commit to repay $1,093,231 to the Cardano Treasury through a revenue-share mechanism using 25% of fees until full reimbursement, then 5% permanently, with quarterly public reporting.
Milestone gating, contingency return, independent audit, oversight review, quarterly reporting, and undisbursed funds remaining under Treasury control are presented as treasury protections.
The proposal states that the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at submission.
The document states that Anvil/Sellout have not received ADA from the Cardano Treasury within the last 24 months.

summary: The anchor describes a 4,969,231 ADA treasury withdrawal for an 8-month Phase 2 enterprise ticketing build with milestone-gated delivery, Intersect administration, projected adoption metrics, and a proposed revenue-share repayment mechanism, but many key adoption, contract, repayment, feasibility, and track-record claims are asserted rather than evidenced in the document.
